messages.content: The PNW hosts finally firmed up times. Salem moved earlier Tuesday, Eugene confirmed the Wednesday transfer fair ends at 8:30, and Corvallis is still Thursday late morning. Can you rank the flight/routing plans and tell me where I should actually sleep?

Yes. The key trade-off is Thursday: an Eugene return saves driving after Corvallis, but only if the connection is not rushed. Send me the flight quotes you have and I will rank them with the hotel bases.

Option A is SLC to PDX Sunday afternoon, then EUG to SLC Thursday with a 43-minute Seattle layover, $456. Option B is PDX round trip, Sunday afternoon in and Thursday 5:15 pm back, $392. Option C is the same open-jaw but the EUG return has a 78-minute Seattle layover, $486. Rental is about $40 more for one-way drop at EUG.

My ranking: 1. Option C, open-jaw with the 78-minute Seattle layover. It costs more, but it protects Thursday and avoids the Corvallis-to-Portland drive before a flight. 2. Option B, PDX round trip. Use this if reimbursement pushes back on the higher airfare and one-way rental. The drawback is a long drive after the Corvallis coffee, with Portland traffic uncertainty. 3. Option A, cheaper EUG return with 43 minutes in Seattle. I would list it only as priced but not recommended.
Okay. For Sunday and Monday, would you stay near the Portland fair venue or in Vancouver? The venue hotels have paid parking and no breakfast, but Vancouver adds traffic.

I would stay Vancouver or north/east Vancouver Sunday and Monday, then plan the Monday fair drive deliberately. Since you have the Vancouver counselor breakfast Monday, the free breakfast and parking are useful, and you can avoid moving hotels that day. For the Portland fair, leave the hotel early, preselect a garage near the venue, and treat the parking fee as part of the fair cost. I would only switch to a venue hotel if load-in is unusually early or parking becomes impossible.
Tuesday night is the bigger question. Salem/Keizer after the morning visits, or push to Eugene?

Push to Eugene Tuesday night. Because Salem starts early, you should be done early enough to drive south before dinner. Staying in Eugene Tuesday gives you a calmer Wednesday, lets you check the fair location ahead of time, and avoids a morning I-5 drive with materials in the car.
What about breakfast timing before the early Salem visit?

For Tuesday, choose the Vancouver hotel only if breakfast starts by 6:00 or has grab-and-go available by 6:30. If not, plan a coffee-and-bagel stop on the way to Salem. For Eugene, breakfast is more useful Wednesday and Thursday, but Thursday you should keep it quick because of the Corvallis coffee.
Which refundable rooms should I hold first while approval finishes?

Hold these in order: first, a Vancouver-area hotel for Sunday and Monday with free parking, breakfast, and a queen non-smoking room. Second, an Eugene or Springfield hotel for Tuesday and Wednesday with breakfast, easy parking, and restaurants close enough for after the Wednesday fair. Third, a backup Portland venue hotel for Monday only, refundable, in case the organizer later says load-in or parking will be difficult. I would not hold Salem unless the Tuesday schedule runs much later than expected.
Give me the clean recommendation I can put in the approval note.

Recommendation: approve SLC-PDX Sunday afternoon and EUG-SLC Thursday with the 78-minute Seattle connection, plus the one-way rental drop at EUG. Do not use the 43-minute connection. Hotel plan: Vancouver-area base Sunday/Monday for the counselor breakfast and parking/breakfast value; Eugene/Springfield Tuesday/Wednesday to protect the Wednesday fair and Thursday Corvallis timing. Note the higher airfare is offset by avoiding a Thursday drive from Corvallis to Portland and reducing missed-connection risk.

messages.content: Approval came through for the PNW loop. Let’s move it from plan to actual reservations: Sunday afternoon into Portland, rental car, Vancouver Sunday and Monday, Eugene Tuesday and Wednesday, and the calmer EUG return Thursday.

Great. I will set this up as one ticket where possible: SLC-PDX Sunday Sep 15 in the afternoon, then EUG-SEA-SLC Thursday Sep 19 with the longer Seattle connection. Before I lock details, do you want the pay-later rental and window seats requested on all legs if available?
Yes. Pay-later rental, window seats if I can get them, queen non-smoking rooms. Breakfast timing matters on the hotel side.

Flights are set for the booking summary: Delta SLC-PDX Sun Sep 15, 2:55 pm to 4:05 pm, window seat requested. Return is EUG-SEA-SLC Thu Sep 19, departing Eugene 2:30 pm, Seattle connection about 80 minutes, arriving Salt Lake City 7:50 pm. I marked the 43-minute option as not selected.
Good. For hotels, I have a Hampton in Vancouver and a Holiday Inn Express in Springfield/Eugene showing refundable. Can you confirm the practical stuff?

Yes. Vancouver Hampton: queen non-smoking, free breakfast starting 6:00 on weekdays, free parking, Wi-Fi included, cancel by Sat Sep 14 at 6:00 pm local time. Nearby dinner options are a short drive, so it works better as a quiet base than a walkable evening area. Eugene/Springfield Holiday Inn Express: queen non-smoking, breakfast 6:30 to 9:30, free parking, Wi-Fi included, cancel by Mon Sep 16 at 6:00 pm local time. There are several easy restaurants near Gateway and I-5 for the late Wednesday return.
Book those two. Any issue using Vancouver for the Monday Portland fair?

It is fine if you build in the buffer. Plan to leave the Vancouver hotel around 3:45 for a 5:00 load-in, earlier if weather or traffic looks bad. Use a garage near the venue rather than circling surface lots with the banner and boxes.
Rental car details next. I need space for the banner tube and two material boxes, but not a huge vehicle.

Reserve the intermediate SUV, pay-later: pickup PDX Sunday at 4:45 pm, return EUG Thursday at about 1:15 pm. Unlimited mileage, one-way drop included in the quoted total, and enough cargo space for luggage, banner tube, and boxes without moving up to a full-size SUV.
Can you put the whole Sunday-to-Thursday timeline in one place?

Timeline: Sunday, fly SLC-PDX 2:55-4:05, pick up rental around 4:45, drive to Vancouver hotel, dinner nearby. Monday, breakfast at hotel, Vancouver counselor breakfast, afternoon prep, leave 3:45 for Portland fair parking and load-in, return to Vancouver after the fair. Tuesday, breakfast early, check out, Salem visits beginning 8:15, drive to Eugene/Springfield after the final visit, check in and have dinner near the hotel. Wednesday, Eugene appointments and transfer fair ending 8:30, dinner near hotel or mobile order. Thursday, quick breakfast, drive to Corvallis for late-morning coffee, leave Corvallis by about 11:45, fuel and return car at EUG, fly home at 2:30.
Now give me the reimbursement note for the airfare comparison.

Use this: Comparable PDX round trip was lower, but approved routing is SLC-PDX outbound and EUG-SLC return because Thursday includes a Corvallis commitment and an Eugene departure avoids an added drive to Portland before the flight. The selected return also uses the longer Seattle connection rather than the lower-cost 43-minute option. Attach screenshots for the PDX round trip, the rejected tight-connection EUG fare, the selected EUG fare, and the one-way rental quote.
Perfect. Final booking summary, including cancellation cutoffs and receipts I should save?

Final summary: Delta SLC-PDX Sun Sep 15 2:55-4:05, window requested; EUG-SEA-SLC Thu Sep 19 2:30-7:50, longer Seattle connection, window requested. Pay-later intermediate SUV, PDX pickup Sun 4:45, EUG return Thu 1:15, one-way fee included. Hotels: Vancouver Hampton Sun/Mon, queen non-smoking, breakfast 6:00 weekdays, free parking, cancel by Sep 14 at 6:00 pm; Eugene/Springfield Holiday Inn Express Tue/Wed, queen non-smoking, breakfast 6:30-9:30, free parking, cancel by Sep 16 at 6:00 pm. Save receipts for airfare, rental car, fuel, hotel folios, hotel incidentals if any, Portland fair parking, and any checked-box or baggage fees.

messages.content: One week out and Delta shifted the Eugene connection by about twenty minutes. Also the Portland fair organizer says surface lots may fill before evening load-in. Can you sanity-check the plan?
Yes. What is the new Seattle connection time showing?
EUG-SEA now gets in at 3:55 and SEA-SLC still leaves at 4:55. Same ticket. The Portland return would cost a lot more now.

Keep the Eugene return. A 60-minute Seattle connection on one ticket is not luxurious, but it is still workable and much better than reworking to Portland at a higher fare. I would only reconsider if it drops below about 55 minutes, changes terminals awkwardly, or the first leg moves later again.
Update Thursday timing for me, then. I do not want to be casual about EUG.

Thursday: Corvallis coffee 10:30 to about 11:30. Leave by 11:45, no later than noon. Drive to Eugene airport, fuel before the airport if needed, return the car by 1:15, and be inside by 1:25 for the 2:45 departure. Keep the boarding pass and rental return receipt handy.
For Portland fair parking, should I prepay anything?

Yes, reserve a garage space near the venue for Monday, ideally cancellable or changeable, arrival around 4:15 and exit around 9:30. Do not rely on surface lots with the banner and boxes. Budget about $25-35 and save the receipt.
Last pieces: hotel cancellation cutoffs, dinner after Eugene, and a materials checklist.

Cutoffs: Vancouver hotel cancel by Sep 14 at 6:00 pm; Eugene/Springfield hotel cancel by Sep 16 at 6:00 pm. Keep both. Eugene dinner backup: after the Wednesday fair, go straight back toward the hotel and use a nearby restaurant or mobile order, not a new downtown search with materials. Checklist: ID, university card, flight and hotel confirmations, rental confirmation, fair scanner or tablet, chargers, portable battery, banner tube, tablecloth, brochures, counselor packets, business cards, pens, comfortable shoes, rain layer, water bottle, receipt folder, and a small tote for Thursday coffee materials.
